children: Chinese pharmaceutical major Fosun Pharma has once again trimmed its stake in Gland Pharma, reducing its holding below 50 percent and reviving questions around its long-term plans for the Hyderabad-based injectable drugmaker.

Earlier this month, Fosun’s Singapore unit sold a 6 percent stake in Gland Pharma through block deals and open-market transactions for about $294 million (around Rs 2,800 crore), taking its holding to 45.76 percent from 51.76 percent. The latest sale comes two years after the Chinese company abandoned plans for a complete exit from Gland due to valuation disagreements with prospective buyers and geopolitical concerns around Chinese investments in India.
The investment in Gland is one of the biggest made by a Chinese company in India.
Proceeds to fund Fosun's R&D, share repurchases, debt reduction

In a statement announcing a HK$1 billion share repurchase programme, Fosun said proceeds from the Gland stake sale would be used for “R&D investments, share repurchases and repayment of interest-bearing debts”. The company added that it remains “fully confident in Gland Pharma’s long-term development and its enduring role as a key engine for overseas value creation.”

The transaction coincides with a series of positive developments at Gland Pharma, including the appointment of Deepak Sapra as CEO-designate and a clean USFDA inspection at its Visakhapatnam sterile oncology facility with no Form 483 observations. Sapra was heading the API and CDMO business at Dr. Reddy's.

The latest transaction marks the continuation of a gradual reduction rather than an outright exit. Fosun acquired control of Gland Pharma in 2016, initially agreeing to buy 86 percent for $1.26 billion before restructuring the transaction to acquire a 74 percent stake to comply with India’s foreign investment rules.

Its ownership declined to about 57.9 percent after Gland’s Rs 6,480 crore IPO in 2020, then to 51.8 percent following a 6 percent block sale in June 2024, and now to 45.76 percent after the latest disposal.
Analysts view the sale largely as a capital allocation exercise by Fosun rather than a reflection of any deterioration in Gland’s business fundamentals.

The Chinese company had faced debt-related pressures during 2022-23 and explored selling its entire Gland stake. While deleveraging has eased, Fosun is now monetising part of its investment after a sharp rally in Gland shares. Gland’s stock has gained strongly in 2026, supported by improving earnings, new contract manufacturing wins and a recovery in its core US business.
Brokerages remain broadly constructive on Gland Pharma despite concerns around valuation after the stock’s sharp run-up.

ICICI Securities recently reiterated a “Buy” rating with a target price of Rs 3,150, citing strong growth in the US and Europe, a healthy injectable pipeline, new CDMO contracts and management’s upgraded growth outlook. The brokerage expects revenue growth of 18-20 percent over the next several years and sees Gland benefiting from increasing opportunities in complex injectables and contract manufacturing.

Elara Capital is also positive on the company’s operating performance but turned more cautious on valuations after the share price surged about 40 percent in three months. The brokerage downgraded the stock to “Accumulate” from “Buy”, saying Gland’s growth momentum remains intact but management’s target of a 20 percent revenue CAGR over four years appears ambitious.

The favourable analyst view comes as Gland continues to deliver strong operational updates. The company reported nearly 20 percent revenue growth in the June quarter, driven by demand in the US market and its expanding contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) business. It has also secured new CDMO contracts, including in GLP-1 therapies, and recently entered a manufacturing agreement with a global pharmaceutical company that could generate annual revenue of $90 million to $100 million once fully commercialised.

title: Fosun sale raises questions, but brokerages back Gland Pharma growth outlook
